answer: The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 26% of the resulting slash, which forfeits for adversarial review out of the adversary's own capital. Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the ocean reward in the sonnet ledger costs the operator directly, and the saffron audit records each payout. A farm of 176 keys therefore funds the parties working against it, so growing the farm makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
